explanation: Three alternating cheek kisses are a common greeting between friends, family, and acquaintances in the Netherlands, especially on birthdays and other celebratory occasions, but it isn't used with strangers or in business settings. Men typically shake hands with other men and with people they don't know well, while women more often exchange cheek kisses with both women and men they're already acquainted with.
local_tip: Offer a handshake by default, and only move to cheek kisses if the other person initiates it or you already know them socially.
regional_note: Cheek kissing is somewhat more common in the southern Netherlands than in the north.

also_check.note: Cheek kissing is a standard greeting, though the number of kisses varies by region, typically two to four.
Physical greetings like cheek kissing are uncommon; a bow is the traditional and expected greeting instead.
One or two cheek kisses are common even among people who've just met, typically starting with the right cheek.
